A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GeoArena and contain readable methods, results, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A.1–A.4. Matching content across relocation, renumbering, and model-name formatting supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original crowd-voting results, a 17-model leaderboard, style-preference analysis, LVLM–human agreement measurements, and appendix dataset analyses and cases.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds an expert-versus-crowd agreement study on 100 examples.

M1.justification: Both retain anonymized pairwise voting, Bradley-Terry fitting for final rankings, and style-adjusted regression. The expanded regression explanation and removal of an online-Elo implementation sentence do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both use GeoArena/GeoArena-1K for worldwide image geolocalization and response-preference evaluation. The expert audit samples existing examples; dataset composition and the appendix case coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The new voting-reliability experiment introduces expert annotations as a human reference for crowd votes (v3 Table 4). The 17 leaderboard models and the Gemini/Qwen LVLM-judge comparison remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds a protocol reviewing 100 randomly sampled examples using anonymized responses and tool-assisted expert judgments, taking approximately 3–5 minutes each. Reported deployment increases from two to three months, without establishing that the retained September leaderboard was rerun.

E4.justification: v3 Section 4.3 adds direct validation of crowd-vote quality against expert judgments. The existing style analysis, LVLM alignment study, hard-case analysis, and additional geographic case studies are retained.

E5.justification: v1 already reports bootstrap-based 95% confidence intervals; v3 Section 4.1 newly specifies 100 bootstrap rounds. The intervals are unchanged, and this disclosure does not establish an increase in resampling or experimental runs.

E6.justification: v3 Table 4 adds expert/crowd agreement counts and 78.0% overall agreement. Leaderboard scores and intervals, heatmaps, style coefficients, model-judge accuracies of 0.6579 and 0.4667, and appendix composition values remain unchanged. v3 also drops the prose claim of Gemma improvement from 4B to 27B.

T1.justification: The Elo and Bradley-Terry probabilities, likelihood, score transformation, and static-capability assumption remain mathematically equivalent. Some equations become inline or are renumbered; no substantive definition, derivation, or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract adds an explicit claim that GeoArena has been open-sourced. The central contributions—dynamic preference-based benchmarking, voting-data analysis, and dataset release—retain their meaning; replacing 'human-centered' with 'user-preference-based' largely clarifies terminology.

C2.justification: v3 interprets expert/crowd agreement as supporting voting reliability. It removes v1's caution about extreme win rates from sparsely sampled matchups and the specific explanation that Qwen struggles to capture nuanced human criteria. Most other interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a repository link and reproducibility/ethics disclosures covering code, data, consent, and data handling. It newly documents manual prompt filtering and normalized logistic-regression style features, while omitting timestamps from the documented collection fields. These disclosures do not establish changes to retained experiments.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including GLOBE, GAGA, GOMAA-Geo, and GeoAI/reward-model surveys, while removing the generic LVLM related-work paragraph. Table 1 replaces the privacy-preserving comparison property with user-preference-based evaluation; the central positioning against static benchmarks remains.

P1.justification: v3 standardizes model names and terminology, rearranges the introduction's workflow explanation, trims commentary, and adds reliability, ethics, and reproducibility sections. The author name Yixuan Li becomes Sharon Li. Most prose and the overall document structure remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v3 adds the expert-agreement table, converts v1 Figure 5's doughnut charts into Table 7 with identical values, and reformats the LVLM-alignment table. The leaderboard moves, chart labels and sizing change, and appendix case figures are renumbered without changing their content.

improvement.justification: The 100-example expert audit (v3 Table 4, 78% agreement) adds direct support for crowd-vote reliability, while bootstrap and access disclosures improve documentation. These gains are limited by unspecified expert-annotator details, removal of the sparse-match caution, and obsolete doughnut-chart descriptions beside Appendix Table 7.
